title: Goats Climb a 160-Foot Dam Straight Up. Here's Why

scenes.text: Goats climb a 160 foot dam. Straight up.
It's the Cingino Dam in northern Italy, and the wall is almost vertical.
The goats are Alpine ibex, and they're after salt.
Their plant diet lacks minerals, and dam concrete may hold salty deposits.
The rough wall gives their hooves just enough grip.
Big males don't try. Their horns and weight make balance too hard.
A wall built for water. Climbed for salt.

description:
Goats climb a 160 foot dam. Straight up.
Alpine ibex scale the almost vertical Cingino Dam in northern Italy to lick salt and minerals from the wall.
